title: Close the three feature-close-review allow regressions: mv source, cd redirect swallow, cp -t separator eat
judge_obligation_ack: fix cell from the feature-close independent review itself; delta re-verified before merge

truths: mv extracts BOTH its source operands and its destination (and with -t: the dir plus every source) — mv .bee/state.json /tmp/x is denied again by the direct-edit guard, and an mv of a reservation-held source raises the conflict; cp keeps sources dropped

cd . > <protected-file> is denied again: the cd segment-consume loop still routes redirect operators through match_redirect (or stops at the first redirect), so a redirect target inside a cd segment is extracted

cp -t followed by a separator no longer eats it: the -t/--target-directory lookahead refuses a separator token, the loop stops at the separator, and the NEXT command's targets are extracted — cp -t ; rm -rf .bee/state.json is denied again

action: Fix three P1 allow-regressions found by the feature-close review, all in guards.rs extract_bash_targets: (1) split the cp/mv operand-role rule — cp drops sources (keep wgh-1 behavior and its tests), mv extracts every operand (sources are unlinked, so they are writes; retarget tests.rs:2455-area pins that currently assert mv source-dropping, red-first); (2) in the wgh-4 cd segment-consume loop (guards.rs:662-677) run each consumed token through match_redirect so a redirect and its file inside a cd segment still extract (or stop consuming at the first redirect operator); (3) guard the -t/--target-directory lookahead (guards.rs:780-788) with an is_separator check so a separator is never taken as the argument and the scan resumes at the separator. Red-first regression tests for all three concrete inputs above plus mv -t parity.
acceptance: All three must_haves truths hold with named tests; every pre-branch denial in these three shapes denies again; suite green

trace.outcome: Closed the three P1 allow-regressions: mv now extracts every operand (source+dest), a redirect inside a cd segment still extracts, and -t/--target-directory never eats a following separator
